summary: The source permits at most ten asynchronous functions and ten pool slots, while correctness depends on start order, the pending-promise safety limit, work-conserving refill, and eventual completion rather than scalable wall-clock growth.

workload_bound.source_constraint: functions.length is between zero and ten and the pool limit n is between one and ten

replacement_checks.evidence: At most min(m, n) workers are created; each of the m indices is claimed once, invoked once, and awaited once before its worker can claim another index.
Authored schedules cover zero and ten functions, pool limits one and above the work count, equal finishes, zero-duration work, and repeated refill by the fastest slot.

The deterministic app adapter records every start and finish time, completion time, and maximum pending count so cases verify input start order, the n-promise cap, immediate refill, and complete execution.
The exact native worker source is remotely Accepted under the provider timeout, while every local schedule case deterministically reaches zero remaining work and a finite completion time.
